description: Hand-written evaluation cases for the evidence gates, written from evals/cases/SPEC.md and shaped by evals/cases/SCHEMA.md without reference to any implementation. Each entry under 'files' is the complete content of the named per-gate case file. All people, employers and statements are fictional. Frozen once its SHA-256 is recorded in spec_suite_v1.sha256.

cases.sense: claim: states the candidate's own diagnosis

record.text: Managed a type 2 diabetes diagnosis while working full-time rotating shifts.

cases.rationale: The record discloses the candidate's own medical diagnosis, a sensitive personal attribute that must be kept out of automated use.

cases.sense: harmless: diagnosed technical faults

record.text: Diagnosed intermittent network faults across 14 branch offices using packet captures.

cases.rationale: Diagnosed refers to finding technical faults, so this is ordinary work evidence with no personal attribute.

cases.sense: claim: states the candidate's own disability (noun)

record.text: Met every quarterly sales target while living with a physical disability.

cases.rationale: The record discloses that the candidate has a disability, which is a sensitive personal attribute.

cases.sense: harmless: disability access standards in professional work

record.text: Audited the council website against disability access guidelines and fixed 40 issues.

cases.rationale: Disability names an accessibility standard the candidate worked to, not an attribute of the candidate.

cases.sense: claim: describes the candidate as disabled (adjective)

record.text: Returned to a full caseload as a disabled employee after a spinal injury.

cases.rationale: The record describes the candidate as disabled and refers to an injury, both sensitive health attributes.

cases.sense: harmless: disabled user accounts in a system

record.text: Disabled 200 dormant user accounts in Active Directory during the quarterly access review.

cases.rationale: Disabled is an administrative action on computer accounts, so the record is harmless work evidence.

cases.sense: claim: describes the candidate as autistic (adjective)

record.text: Autistic analyst who brings close attention to detail to data-quality checks.

cases.rationale: The record states that the candidate is autistic, which is neurodivergence and therefore a sensitive attribute.

record.text: Designed quiet-hour gallery sessions for autistic visitors with the museum learning team.

cases.rationale: The word describes the visitors served by the work, not the candidate, so no personal attribute is disclosed.

cases.persona: Care assistant in a residential home who also builds the staff rota.

job.title: Senior Care Assistant
job.description: We are looking for a senior care assistant to lead shifts in a 40-bed home. You will resolve concerns raised by residents and their families, review daily care records to spot changes in residents' needs, and check medication records carefully for accuracy. Experience writing care plans is essential.

evidence.text: Supported 12 residents with personal care, meals and medication prompts on day shifts.
Wrote and updated care plans with residents and their families each month.
Built the weekly staff rota in Excel for 22 care workers.
Resolved concerns raised by relatives by phone and arranged follow-up meetings with the manager.
Trained four new starters in moving and handling procedures.

cases.rationale: The evidence is direct care, care planning and handling relatives' concerns, which supports customer-facing problem-solving and both listed tools but no technical, quantitative or analytical work.

cases.persona: Retail supervisor in a high-street clothing store.

job.title: Retail Data Analyst
job.description: Join our trading team to analyse store and online sales. You will automate weekly reports with Python, build and test data pipelines that feed our dashboards, and work with store teams to understand and fix problems they raise.

evidence.text: Supervised a team of eight sales assistants across weekday and weekend shifts.
Handled customer refunds and complaints at the service desk, resolving most on the spot.
Counted stock weekly and reported shrinkage figures to the area manager.
Set out seasonal displays to head-office layouts.
Opened and closed the store, including cashing up and banking the takings.

cases.rationale: The evidence shows shop-floor supervision and customer complaint handling but never mentions Excel, Power BI, analysis or any technical work, so only customer-facing problem-solving is supported.

cases.persona: School office administrator at a primary school.

job.title: Office Manager
job.description: The office manager will be the first point of contact for families, use spreadsheets to analyse attendance patterns across the trust, and move paper processes into streamlined digital workflows.

evidence.text: Answered telephone and front-desk enquiries from parents for a primary school of 420 pupils.
Kept pupil attendance registers up to date and followed up unexplained non-attendance with families by phone.
Produced the weekly parent newsletter in Microsoft Word.
Ordered classroom supplies within a termly budget of £6,000.
Booked supply teachers from the agency list to cover staff leave.

cases.rationale: The evidence is front-office work with parents and one use of Word; it does not show Excel, Outlook, analysis or automation, so only customer problem-solving and Word are supported.

cases.persona: Volunteer coordinator at a charity shop.

job.title: Community Engagement Officer
job.description: You will look after our supporters and volunteers and sort out any issues they bring to us, analyse fundraising and volunteer figures to guide decisions, and help automate our supporter emails.

evidence.text: Recruited and inducted 30 volunteers for a charity shop over two years.

Sorted and priced donated stock, raising about £1,200 a week.
Posted weekly updates about new stock on the shop's Facebook page.

cases.rationale: The evidence shows volunteer management, social media posting and customer questions at the till, supporting both tools and customer problem-solving but nothing technical or analytical.

cases.persona: Hotel receptionist at a city-centre hotel.

job.title: Guest Experience Coordinator
job.description: Resolve guest issues quickly and fairly, analyse guest feedback scores to find recurring problems, test our new booking platform before launch, and help introduce AI chat assistants for guest messaging.

evidence.text: Checked in up to 80 guests a day at a 120-room city hotel.
Resolved booking errors and room complaints at the front desk, offering upgrades within agreed limits.
Took reservations by phone and email in English and French.
Balanced the front-desk float at the end of each shift.

cases.rationale: The evidence shows guest-facing problem-solving and use of French, but never names Opera PMS or any analysis, testing or AI work, so only customer problem-solving is supported.

cases.persona: Payroll clerk in a mid-sized manufacturing firm.

job.title: Payroll and Systems Officer

job.title: Tenancy Sustainment Officer

evidence.text: Managed a patch of 350 council tenancies, carrying out annual home visits.
Agreed affordable repayment arrangements with tenants in rent arrears, reducing arrears on the patch by 15 per cent.
Mediated disputes between neighbours and referred serious cases to the antisocial behaviour team.
Explained tenancy rights and responsibilities to new tenants at sign-up.
Recorded visits and actions in the housing management system within 48 hours.

cases.rationale: The evidence is tenant-facing casework and negotiation, which supports customer problem-solving and both tools; recording visits in a system is not technical or analytical work.

evidence.text: Coordinated 45 weddings a year at a country-house venue, from first viewing to the day itself.

cases.persona: Contact-centre adviser for an energy supplier.

job.title: Customer Insight Analyst
job.description: Analyse call and complaint data to find the root causes of customer problems, trial AI tools that summarise calls, and work with advisers to solve customer issues first time.

evidence.text: Handled about 60 inbound calls a day about energy bills and meter readings.
Set up affordable payment arrangements for customers in debt.
Logged every call and follow-up action in Salesforce.
Resolved escalated complaints within the eight-week regulatory deadline.
Coached two new advisers during their first month on the phones.

cases.rationale: The evidence is customer calls, complaints and case logging in Salesforce, supporting customer problem-solving and the tools but not data analysis or AI tools.

cases.persona: Junior data analyst in an insurance claims team.

job.title: Insurance Data Analyst
job.description: Use SQL and Python to analyse claims data, automate recurring reports, and check figures carefully against finance totals before they are published.

evidence.text: Wrote SQL queries to extract monthly claims data from the underwriting database.
Automated the weekly claims summary with a Python script scheduled on the team server.
Built Power BI dashboards on claim volumes for the operations director.
Checked query results against finance ledger totals before each dashboard release.
Explained trends in claim volumes to non-technical managers at monthly reviews.

cases.rationale: The analyst writes SQL and Python, automates a report and validates figures, but has no integration work or customer contact and never uses Tableau, so the broad software-development statement is not supported.

cases.persona: Back-end developer on a council permit service.

job.title: Software Engineer
job.description: Build Python services for public-facing applications, integrate with payment and identity APIs, and write automated tests that run on every change.

evidence.text: Built Django REST endpoints for a council permit application service.
Integrated the service with a card payment provider's API and handled its webhook callbacks.
Wrote pytest suites for the permit workflow and ran them in the CI pipeline on every merge.
Designed PostgreSQL tables and migrations for permit and payment records.
Containerised the service with Docker for deployment to the shared test environment.

cases.rationale: The evidence covers building Django services, integrating a payment API and writing tests, so the technical statement holds, but there is no customer contact, analysis or AWS use.

cases.persona: Research technician in a university optics laboratory.

job.title: Research Software Engineer
job.description: Develop Python software to control instruments and analyse experimental data, automate measurement workflows, and validate results against reference measurements.

evidence.text: Calibrated laser interferometers for a university optics research group.
Wrote Python scripts to fit decay curves to photodetector data and estimate measurement uncertainty.
Built a LabVIEW control program that stepped a translation stage and logged readings automatically.
Co-authored a peer-reviewed paper on thermal noise in optical cavities.
Tested the data-acquisition rig against reference signals before each experimental run.

cases.rationale: The technician builds and tests instrument-control software within published physics research, supporting the technical and quantitative statements, but MATLAB is never used and there is no customer work.

cases.persona: IT support technician who automates account and device set-up.

job.title: IT Automation Engineer
job.description: Automate service desk workflows, integrate the IT service management tool with directory and device management systems, test changes safely before roll-out and keep users informed.

evidence.text: Resolved 25 to 30 hardware and software tickets a day for staff across three hospital sites.
Wrote PowerShell scripts to create new starter accounts and mailboxes, cutting set-up time from an hour to ten minutes.
Enrolled 600 laptops in Microsoft Intune and tested compliance policies on a pilot group first.
Integrated the ServiceNow catalogue with Active Directory so approved access requests were applied automatically.
Talked staff through fixes by phone and closed tickets with clear notes.

cases.rationale: The evidence shows scripting, a ServiceNow integration, piloted policy testing and user-facing support, but never Python or any quantitative research.

cases.persona: Software tester on an online banking app.

job.title: QA Engineer
job.description: Write automated tests in Python, test integrations between our payment APIs, and validate every release against acceptance criteria.

evidence.text: Wrote and ran manual test scripts for each release of an online banking app.
Automated 150 regression tests in Selenium with Java, cutting the regression run from two days to three hours.
Tested REST APIs with Postman collections, including error and timeout cases.
Logged defects in Jira with clear reproduction steps and retested each fix.
Checked that new screens could be used with a screen reader before release.

cases.rationale: The tester writes automated tests in Java and tests other people's APIs, which supports testing, but testing an integration is not building one, so the development-integration-testing statement is unsupported, and there is no Python, JavaScript or customer work.

cases.persona: Engineer building a language-model email triage service.

job.title: AI Engineer
job.description: Build Python services that use large language models, integrate them with third-party APIs, automate support workflows and evaluate model quality with care.

evidence.text: Built a Python service that classifies incoming customer emails with a language model and routes them to the right team.
Called the OpenAI API with structured prompts and validated its JSON output against a schema before use.
Evaluated the classifier on 2,000 hand-labelled emails and reported precision and recall for each category.
Integrated the routing service with the Zendesk API so that tickets were tagged automatically.
Wrote SQL to pull historical ticket data for the training and evaluation sets.

cases.rationale: The evidence shows building, integrating and evaluating a language-model service, but it is not physics or scientific research, involves no customer contact and never uses LangChain.

cases.persona: Front-end web developer at a small agency.

job.title: Front-End Developer
job.description: Build accessible websites, integrate forms with third-party APIs, test across browsers and work directly with clients to fix issues.

evidence.text: Built responsive page templates in React for three charity websites.
Themed and maintained WordPress sites for 12 small business clients.
Met clients to agree page layouts and fixed issues they reported after launch.
Wrote JavaScript to connect contact forms to a mailing-list provider's API.
Tested each site across browsers and screen sizes before handover.

cases.rationale: The developer builds, integrates and tests websites and works directly with clients, but never uses Figma, Python or any analytical methods.

cases.persona: Finance data engineer who automated the month-end close.

job.title: Finance Systems Developer
job.description: Automate finance processes in Python, integrate banking APIs with our data warehouse, analyse process performance and test every change.

evidence.text: Replaced a spreadsheet-based month-end process with Python jobs scheduled in Airflow.
Pulled bank transactions through the bank's API and loaded them into the finance data warehouse.
Wrote SQL reconciliation checks that flagged unmatched transactions for the accounts team.
Added unit tests for each transformation step and ran them before deployment.
Analysed month-end timings and cut the close from eight working days to five.

cases.rationale: The evidence shows Python development, API integration, tests and process analysis, but Excel is never named, there is no customer contact and no scientific research.

cases.persona: Research assistant in freshwater environmental science.

job.title: Environmental Data Scientist
job.description: Analyse water-quality data with statistical models, write tested Python tools for sensor data, and present findings to operational teams.

evidence.text: Collected river water samples monthly and measured nitrate levels in the laboratory.
Fitted mixed-effects models in R to relate nitrate levels to rainfall and land use.
Wrote a Python package that cleans logger data and flags sensor drift, with unit tests for each rule.
Mapped sampling sites and catchments in QGIS for the project reports.
Presented findings to farmers and the local water company at catchment meetings.

cases.rationale: The researcher does environmental science with statistical models and a tested Python package, which supports quantitative research as a capability, but the quantitative statement claims a grounding in physics that the evidence lacks, there is no integration work for the software statement, presenting to farmers is not customer-facing work and SPSS is never used.

cases.persona: Embedded engineer on a vehicle battery monitoring board.

job.title: Embedded Software Engineer
job.description: Write firmware in C, integrate controllers over CAN bus, and build automated test rigs in Python to validate every production board.

evidence.text: Wrote C firmware for a battery monitoring board on an ARM microcontroller.
Integrated the board with the vehicle's CAN bus and decoded messages from the motor controller.
Built a Python test harness that ran 300 automated checks on each production board.
Traced intermittent faults with an oscilloscope and logic analyser.
Documented test procedures for the production line.

cases.rationale: The engineer develops firmware, integrates hardware and builds a Python test harness, supporting the technical statement and all tools, but the work is engineering rather than scientific research and involves no customers or APIs.

cases.persona: Astrophysics PhD graduate moving into data science.

job.title: Quantitative Researcher
job.description: Apply statistical and physical modelling to market data, write reliable Python analysis code, and validate models rigorously before use.

evidence.text: Measured galaxy rotation curves from telescope spectra during a PhD in astrophysics.
Wrote Python pipelines with NumPy to reduce 12 terabytes of survey data.
Estimated uncertainties with Markov chain Monte Carlo methods and published three first-author papers.
Validated the pipeline against simulated data with known inputs before each survey release.
Queried the survey archive in SQL to select targets for follow-up observations.

cases.rationale: The evidence is physics research with Python pipelines and validation, strongly supporting the quantitative statement, but with no integration work the software statement is unsupported, and TensorFlow is never used.
